# Long-term reanalysis-based energy yield of the Gulf of Saros offshore wind candidate area, Türkiye: sensitivity to reference period, grid node and wind data source

## Abstract

Türkiye published four candidate areas for offshore wind in May 2026. For the
Gulf of Saros area, this study asks what a public reanalysis indicates about
the long-term energy yield, and how sensitive the answer is to choices that
are often left implicit. Hourly ERA5 wind speeds for 1994–2024 at the grid
node nearest the candidate polygon were extrapolated to a hub height of 105 m
and converted hour by hour with a reference 9.5 MW power curve and assumed
losses. The net specific yield is about 2.35 GWh MW⁻¹ yr⁻¹, at a net capacity
factor of about 27 %. The 90 % sampling confidence interval of the 31-year
mean is ±2.3 %. The two neighbouring ERA5 output nodes give +6.7 % and −8.5 %;
these differences recur in every year and are several times larger than that
interval. The node used lies outside the polygon, at a point of strong land
influence in the model. The Global Wind Atlas indicates a mean wind speed
about 12 % higher than ERA5 over the atlas's mesoscale simulation period.
Model data cannot resolve this disagreement, because the atlas is driven by
ERA5. The most recent 11 years alone give a yield 3.1 % higher than the
31-year mean. This observed difference is of the same size as the sampling
uncertainty of an 11-year mean (±3.8 %) and does not by itself establish a
lasting change. The categories differ in kind and are reported separately;
they are not combined into one uncertainty interval. A first-order screening
shows water depths below 62 m throughout the polygon and an overlap of about
14 % with a Special Environmental Protection Area. No result is validated
against offshore measurements. For narrow coastal areas, the reference period,
the grid node and the wind product should be reported and tested, and
measurements inside the polygon are the step that would most improve knowledge
of the resource.

**Keywords:** offshore wind energy; ERA5 reanalysis; energy yield; capacity
factor; spatial representativeness; reference period; sensitivity analysis;
Global Wind Atlas; Gulf of Saros; Türkiye
